title: Onprem airgap: offline bundle vendoring for rke2 + ubuntu-22.04 rollback tooling
author: Samira Patel
description: Context: Customers running Redwood Private in air-gapped RKE2 clusters on Ubuntu 22.04 reported upgrade failures during kernel/apt rollouts and missing vendor artifacts for additional distro combinations. This PR prepares a repeatable offline bundle vendoring flow and ships a first-pass rollback toolset for on-prem installations. Motivation: make offline bundles reproducible across rke2 + ubuntu-22.04 environments and provide an automated rollback path for failed upgrades. Changes: 1) Offline bundle vendoring: add apt mirrors, pre-baked deb packages and checksums for ubuntu-22.04; vendor rke2 images and helm charts into the bundle; include TUF metadata and expiry policy; add vendoring scripts (vendoring/ubuntu-22.04/*.sh) to reproduce bundle. 2) Rollback tooling: introduce 'airgap-rollback' CLI wrapper that can fetch the last-good-bundle metadata, restore previous helm release state, and reapply image tarballs; includes idempotent checks and dry-run mode. 3) Helm chart updates: bump private-installer chart to 0.22.1 with backwards-compatible hooks for pre-upgrade validation and post-rollback cleanup. 4) Installer integration: installer adds optional --rollback-on-failure flag and emits structured rollback hints to the audit log. 5) Tests & docs: e2e test matrix additions for rke2+ubuntu-22.04 and a new troubleshooting section in docs/airgap.md. Backwards compatibility: designed to be non-breaking when rollback tooling is disabled by default. Checklist: - [x] Vendored packages added and checksums verified - [x] airgap-rollback basic flow implemented - [x] Helm chart bump and compatibility tests - [x] Integration tests (local rke2 cluster) passing - [x] Docs updated (airgap.md) - [x] Linear/Jira links attached Testing notes: initial CI e2e failed due to missing dpkg dependency in the vendoring script; fixed by adding apt-utils and re-running the mirror job. Manual test instructions: see docs/airgap.md#rollback for reproduction steps (install on Ubuntu 22.04 RKE2, run upgrade, force-failure, run airgap-rollback --dry-run then --apply). Deployment notes: release as part of private-installer v0.22.1; operators should stage the new bundle to their apt mirror and verify TUF root/targets before upgrading.

review_comments: Ethan Liu: please include checksum verification for debs in the installer flow — addressed in vendoring/mirror-setup.sh (added sha256sum checks).
Priya Nandakumar: can we make rollback idempotent for partially-applied helm releases? — added safe-state checks and explicit release history lookup.
Marco Rossi: CI flakes observed on arm64 image loading; can we limit artifact set during test? — updated e2e matrix to run a reduced subset on arm64 and full matrix on amd64.
Samira Patel (author): responded — added sha256 verification and a dry-run mode for safer testing; reran CI after adding apt-utils to mirror script.
release_notes: Onprem/airgap: Add vendoring support for RKE2 + Ubuntu 22.04 offline bundles; introduce airgap-rollback CLI and installer rollback integration; bump private-installer helm chart to 0.22.1. Includes tested e2e scenarios and docs updates.
notes_for_ops: Operators: stage the new offline bundle to your internal apt mirror and verify TUF metadata before applying upgrades. To rollback: run tools/airgap-rollback --bundle <bundle-path> --apply; see docs/airgap.md#rollback for troubleshooting. If using automated pipelines, enable --rollback-on-failure to allow installer to trigger helper hints.
